si_3_author_journal_year: Floris et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
si_4_title: A multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) cohort was used.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: we leveraged the unique, large-scale and deeply phenotyped EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP)

answer.LEAP: normative training and testing (via tenfold cross-validation), and clinical research (case-control comparison, clinical/cognitive associations)

dc_2_purpose_each_dataset.detail: The dataset was used both to train the normative models (using all individuals in a cross-validation framework) and to compare groups and relate brain deviations to clinical/cognitive features.
dc_2_purpose_each_dataset.supporting_text: Normative models were derived in an unbiased manner across the entire sample under tenfold cross-validation ... we tested for group differences in ICs and group separability ... we computed multivariate associations (that is, CCA) between subject loadings and clinical, cognitive measures

model-1.model-name: multimodal FFG model (structure, rs-fMRI, task-fMRI, EEG)

dc_3_healthy_control_number_each_normati.detail: The normative model was trained on the entire sample of 204 individuals (105 NAI, 99 autism) using 10-fold cross-validation. Although the study focuses on 'normative' modeling, the training set included the clinical group to ensure an 'unbiased' derivation of the models.
dc_3_healthy_control_number_each_normati.supporting_text: Applying all exclusion criteria resulted in a sample of 204 individuals (99 autism, 105 nonautistic individuals [NAI]) ... Normative models were derived in an unbiased manner across the entire sample under tenfold cross-validation
dc_3_healthy_control_number_each_normati.location: study_1/44220_2024_349_MOESM1_ESM.pdf.md: Supplementary Methods / Participants; study_1/Floris2024.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modeling
